alt: Boltzmann distribution at one temperature with two activation energies: the catalysed Ea line lies to the left of the uncatalysed Ea line, so the area of the curve beyond it, the molecules with enough energy to react, is larger, while the curve itself is unchanged.
caption: Figure: a catalyst lowers Ea, so more molecules have enough energy; the distribution itself is unchanged

alt: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at two temperatures: both curves start at the origin and have the same area; the higher-temperature curve is lower and broader with its peak to the right, so the area beyond the activation energy Ea (the molecules able to react) is much larger.
caption: Figure: Boltzmann distributions at T₁ and a higher T₂; the area beyond Ea grows with temperature

alt: Energy profile of an exothermic reaction: reactants at a higher energy than products; the catalysed path has a lower peak, so a smaller activation energy, but starts and ends at the same energy levels, so the enthalpy change is unchanged.
caption: Figure: a catalyst lowers the activation energy; reactant and product levels, and ΔH, are the same

alt: Energy profile for homogeneous catalysis: the uncatalysed route has one high peak; the catalysed route has two lower peaks with a dip between them for an intermediate, the catalyst reacting in step 1 and being regenerated in step 2, and both end at the same product energy.
caption: Figure: homogeneous catalysis gives a two-step route with two lower activation energies

alt: Concentration-time curve for a first-order reaction with half-life 345 s starting at 0.0800 mol per dm³: the concentration is 0.0400 at 345 s, 0.0200 at 690 s and 0.0100 at 1035 s, so every half-life is the same length, which proves first order.
caption: Figure: a first-order reaction has a constant half-life (345 s here)

alt: Volume of carbon dioxide against time for 0.300 g of calcium carbonate with excess acid: the curve rises steeply then levels at 72 cm³, and a dashed tangent at t = 0 through (30 s, 54 cm³) has gradient 1.8 cm³ per second, the initial rate.
caption: Figure: gas volume against time; the tangent at t = 0 gives the initial rate (1.8 cm³ s⁻¹)

alt: Two graph panels for orders 0, 1 and 2. Concentration against time: zero order is a straight falling line, first order a curve with constant half-life, second order a curve that flattens more slowly. Rate against concentration: zero order is horizontal, first order a straight line through the origin, second order curves upward.
caption: Figure: concentration-time and rate-concentration graphs for zero, first and second order
